0.headline: EAAA India Alternatives raises Rs 360 crore via anchor book, Rs 1,200-crore IPO to open on October 26
0.heading: EAAA India Alternatives raises Rs 360 crore via anchor book, Rs 1,200-crore IPO to open on October 26
0.intro: EAAA India Alternatives IPO | The Rs 1,200-crore initial public offering will open for public subscription on October 26 with price band at Rs 1,585-1,665 per share.
0.body:
EAAA India Alternatives, the private alternative asset and investment management company-promoted by Edelweiss Group, on Friday raised Rs 360 crore by allocating 21.62 lakh equity shares via anchor book ahead of IPO opening next week.

The Rs 1,200-crore initial public offering, which comprises entirely an offer-for-sale, will open for public subscription on October 26 with price band at Rs 1,585-1,665 per share. The offer will close on October 28.

Promoter entity Edelweiss Securities and Investments will be selling shareholder in the offer-for-sale.

EAAA India Alternatives has announced allocation of 21.62 lakh shares at the upper end of price band. Global investors participated in the anchor book were Government Pension Fund Global, Schroder International, Hornbill Capital Advisors, Goldman Sachs, and BNP Paribas Financial Markets.

"Out of the total allocation to anchor book, the company allocated 14.14 lakh equity shares to 10 domestic mutual funds including HDFC AMC, SBI Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential AMC, Nippon Life India, Kotak Mahindra AMC, Abakkus Asset Manager, HSBC Mutual Fund, and Bandhan Mutual Fund," EAAA India Alternatives in its filing to exchanges said.

As it is entirely an offer-for-sale, the issue proceeds excluding offer expenses will go to selling shareholder, and the company will not receive any funds from the public issue.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

EAAA India Alternatives mainly operates two business verticals - real assets, and private credit along with portfolio management services, managing long term patient capital with an AUM of Rs 95,344.8 crore as of June 2026.

Under the real assets business vertical, the company invests into infrastructure and commercial real estate assets through a mix of equity, quasi-equity and debt instruments, while in private credit business vertical, it provides credit and flexible financing solutions.

Axis Capital, Jefferies India, Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors, and Nuvama Wealth Management are acting as the merchant bankers for the EAAA India Alternatives IPO.

1.headline: Medical devices maker Integris Medtech cuts fresh issue to Rs 600 crore, halves OFS size
1.heading: Medical devices maker Integris Medtech cuts fresh issue to Rs 600 crore, halves OFS size
1.intro: Integris Medtech IPO | The public issue comprises fresh issuance of shares worth Rs 600 crore, and an offer-for-sale of 1.08 crore equity shares.
1.body:
Integris Medtech, the New Delhi-headquartered medical devices and laboratory solutions provider backed by Everstone Capital Asia and ace investor Mukul Agrawal, has reduced the size of its proposed initial public offering (IPO).

As per the notice to investors, the revised IPO will comprise a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 600 crore and an offer-for-sale (OFS) of 1.08 crore equity shares. Promoter entity Evercure Holdings will be the only selling shareholder in the revised OFS, while Gurmit Singh Chugh and Punita Sharma, the company's original promoters, have decided to withdraw from the list of selling shareholders.

&nbsp;

The fresh issue size has been reduced from Rs 925 crore, and an offer-for-sale halved from 2.16 crore equity shares proposed earlier as per the filing of draft document in October 2025. The SEBI approved its IPO papers in February 2026.

Evercure Holdings has also reduced its portion of the OFS from 1.51 crore equity shares.

Integris Medtech has revised the issue size under SEBI regulations that allow a company planning to launch an IPO by March 2027 to increase or reduce the fresh issue size by up to 50% without refiling the draft red herring prospectus (DRHP).

Following the revision, the company, which describes itself as India's second-largest coronary stent manufacturer by sales volume, has also revised the proposed utilisation of proceeds from the fresh issue.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

Accordingly, Rs 509.8 crore will be used to repay debt, while the remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.

With manufacturing facilities in India, Germany and the Netherlands, Integris Medtech has a portfolio of cardiovascular devices, clinical diagnostics and scientific laboratory solutions.

Promoters held an 84.04% stake in the company, as per the DRHP. Evercure Holdings and Medicore Holdings, which are indirectly controlled by Everstone Capital Asia through its role as investment manager of ECP III Pte, held stakes of 28.85% and 33.93%, respectively.

Gurmit Singh Chugh and Punita Sharma, the company's original promoters, each held a 10.23% stake. Evercure Holdings acquired control of the company in 2019 by taking over equity shares from Chugh and Sharma, while Medicore Holdings acquired control through a preferential allotment in the five years immediately preceding the filing of the DRHP.

The book-running lead managers for the proposed Integris Medtech IPO are ICICI Securities, Axis Capital, Citigroup Global Markets India and IIFL Capital Services.

2.headline: Jio IPO sets record with many firsts for an Indian IPO: Here are 7 key milestones
2.heading: Jio IPO sets record with many firsts for an Indian IPO: Here are 7 key milestones
2.intro: Jio IPO became the fastest mega IPO to get fully subscribed and the first globally to receive more than one crore applications.
2.body:
Jio Platforms' initial public offering achieved several milestones during its three-day subscription period from October 21 to 23, including becoming the fastest mega IPO to get fully subscribed and the first globally to receive more than one crore applications.

The issue also set a record as India's largest IPO, with a total size of Rs 30,213 crore, and was the biggest public issue comprising entirely fresh shares.

On the third day of IPO, the issue got subscribed 22.19 times, with investors bidding for over 438 crore shares against 19.75 crore shares on offer, according to NSE data.

Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) led the demand, with their portion subscribed 70.55 times. They bid for over 345.75 crore shares against 4.9 crore shares reserved for the category.

Non-institutional investors (NIIs) subscribed their portion 14 times, bidding for 51.03 crore shares against 3.64 crore shares on offer.

The retail individual investor portion was subscribed 2.72 times, with bids for 23.11 crore shares against 8.5 crore shares reserved.
7 key milestones achieved by Jio Platforms IPO
1) Record public subscription bids: The total demand for the Jio Platforms IPO, including the anchor book, was Rs 7.4 lakh crore.

The IPO received bids from public subscription categories worth more than Rs 4.9 lakh crore, surpassing the comparable demand for LG Electronics India’s 2025 IPO. The milestone made Jio Platforms the most sought-after Indian IPO by the value of bids received outside the anchor investor book, based on publicly available subscription data.

Jio Platforms’ anchor book received bids worth about Rs 2.5 lakh crore for shares worth approximately Rs 8,110 crore allocated to anchor investors. That makes the total stock demand for the IPO at Rs 7 lakh crore. Comparable anchor book figures for other major IPOs are not consistently available publicly, making it difficult to rank offerings on total demand, including anchor investors.

2) First IPO globally to cross one crore applications: Jio Platforms became the first company in global stock market history to receive more than 10 million (one crore) individual investor applications for its IPO.

It surpassed the previous record held by Waaree Energies, which received around 97.3 lakh applications.

3) Largest IPO in Indian corporate history: With an issue size of Rs 30,213 crore, or about $3.2 billion, Jio Platforms' IPO is the largest equity offering in India's history.

The previous record was held by Hyundai Motor India, which raised Rs 27,870 crore, followed by NSE India at Rs 22,561 crore and Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) at Rs 21,008 crore.

4) Biggest IPO comprising entirely fresh shares: The entire Rs 30,213-crore issue comprised fresh 27 crore shares, making it the largest IPO in India to consist entirely of a fresh issue.

Unlike public offerings that include an offer for sale (OFS), allowing existing shareholders to sell their stakes, the Jio Platforms issue did not involve any share sale by parent Reliance Industries or strategic investors Meta and Google.


Check All IPO News
5) Fastest mega IPO to achieve full subscription: The issue was fully subscribed in less than 100 minutes of opening on the first day, making it the fastest mega IPO to reach full subscription.

Previous Indian IPOs worth more than Rs 15,000 crore typically took two to three days to achieve full subscription.

6) First IPO to get extended exchange bidding hours: The BSE and the National Stock Exchange (NSE) extended daily bidding hours for the Jio Platforms IPO to accommodate the high volume of applications.

The exchanges operated from 9 am to 7 pm during the issue period, compared with the usual bidding window of 10 am to 5 pm.

Bidding hours are sometimes extended for large public issues to accommodate investor demand. The NSE IPO had also seen an exception to normal timings to facilitate retail participation.

7) Highest initial market valuation for a newly listed company: At the upper price band of Rs 1,119 per share, Jio Platforms' post-listing market capitalisation is estimated at around Rs 10.3 lakh crore, or about $108 billion.

This would be the highest initial valuation for a newly listed company in India, placing it among the country's top four or five listed companies by market capitalisation on its first day of trading.
